subject: sociology
title: Crime & Subcultures: Cohen's Status Frustration
welcome_lead: Boys without status invert the rules — Cohen explains delinquency.
meta_desc: A-Level Sociology crime subcultures Cohen 1955 status frustration delinquency.
final_note: Working-class boys can't win in school — so they redefine winning.

concepts.def: Group with values distinct from mainstream.
Cohen — failure in mainstream status system breeds resentment.
Merton — gap between goals and means.
Cloward & Ohlin — illegitimate opportunities also differ by area.

walkthroughs.body_html: Cohen (1955) 'Delinquent Boys': working-class boys judged by middle-class teachers find school stacked against them. They suffer status frustration and form a delinquent subculture inverting middle-class values — short-term hedonism, malice, non-utilitarian theft. Vandalism is status reversal in action.

Merton's strain theory explained utilitarian crime (innovation for money). Cohen extended to non-utilitarian crime — joyriding, fighting. Crime gives status group members cannot get from mainstream. Critique: assumes shared starting values; ignores girls (focused on boys).

British youth subcultures (mods, skins, punks, drill rap) echo status reversal — pride in being outsiders. Murray (1990) controversial 'underclass' adds welfare dependency explanation. Messerschmidt (1993): crime is a way of 'doing masculinity' when other routes fail.
